question: Based on the passage, the author would most likely recommend that a restaurant with a long wait for tables:

options.A: give each party an accurate estimate of when its table will be ready.
options.B: offer free music and snacks so that the time passes almost unnoticed.
options.C: seat parties in whatever order makes the dining room run most quickly.
options.D: quote waits a little shorter than expected so customers will not leave.

question: As it is used in paragraph 6, the word "copes" most nearly means:
Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?

options.A: The narrator discovers that a cousin's quick method hides errors that an uncle has to correct.
options.B: The narrator learns that the bank's demand for a figure matters less than the store's own records.
options.C: The narrator decides that counting by hand is the only honest way to take a store's inventory.
options.D: The narrator comes to see that an estimate made with care can be more trustworthy than a careless count.

question: Which detail from the passage best supports the author's claim that a sketchbook is useful "only so long as its owner is willing to let it be bad"?

options.A: Some students no longer draw in the book until they are sure a drawing will work.
options.B: The author uses old sketchbooks to find where a present problem first appeared.
options.C: Painters have long used their sketchbooks for studies, notes, and arithmetic.
options.D: Museums began displaying whole sketchbooks only in about the last hundred years.
